117681.name: Lubavitch of Long Island
117681.note: TorahCafe's biography of Rabbi Tuvia Teldon: 'He first moved to Long Island in 1977 after receiving his Rabbinical Ordination ... As Executive Director of Chabad Lubavitch of Long Island since then'. COLlive (14 July 2023, 'In for the Long Haul'), the Teldons: 'We started off at Stony Brook University' ... 'After six years in Stony Brook, we moved to Commack, in Suffolk County, and opened a shul' (so Commack about 1983); they married on Yud Shevat 1977. Anash: since 1977 the regional directors of Chabad Lubavitch of Long Island.

earlier.where: Stony Brook (they "started off at Stony Brook University")

117685.name: Chabad of Mineola
117685.note: The Jewish Week (JTA site, 18 March 2010): 'Rabbi Perl has been in Mineola since 1990 when he took over the building of a struggling Conservative synagogue on Willis Avenue and renamed it Congregation Beth Sholom Chabad.' The Jewish Star calls him one of the Rebbe's early emissaries on the Island; his earlier work there is not dated here.

117692.name: Chabad of the West Side
117692.note: The Jewish Week (JTA site, 27 March 2018): Rabbi Shlomo Kugel first attracted students 'to a kosher hot dog cart outside the gates of Columbia University in 1984'; Chabad of the West Side 'a fixture in the neighborhood since 1984'. Lubavitch.com (2024): '40 years later'. (A 2026 kollel report quotes him as having founded the center '27 years ago', which does not fit; the 1984 start is in both other sources.)

117901.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Riverdale
117901.note: CrownHeights.info: on Saturday evening, January 23, 2010, a gala 'celebrating the 18th anniversary of Chabad-Lubavitch of Riverdale' (so 1992); the 19th in Jan 2011, the 21st and the 25th ('a quarter century', 2016) agree. Lubavitch.com says the Shemtovs 'set up house here back in 1993'. Rabbi Levi and Sorah Shemtov (Chabad of the Bronx).

117896.name: Chabad of the Five Towns
117896.note: Lubavitch.com (6 Jan 2009): 'Rabbi Zalman and Chanie Wolowik moved here in 1994.' Medium: a Jewish Philanthropy podcast description says they arrived 'in September of 1995' intending to set up a Chabad center, a year later. Now 74 Maple Ave., Cedarhurst.

117665.name: Chabad of Brooklyn Heights
117665.note: Its synagogue, Congregation B'nai Avraham at 117 Remsen Street (the listing's address), founded by Rabbi Aaron Raskin at 21: the Brooklyn Eagle (12 Sept 2012): the neighborhood's only Orthodox synagogue 'has served Brooklyn Heights and Cobble Hill since September 1988'; the congregation's own history: 'officially founded as a religious corporation in December 1988'.

117687.name: Chabad of Great Neck
117687.note: The Jewish Week (JTA site, 8 July 2016): 'Rabbi Geisinsky and his wife, Rebbetzin Chanie Geisinsky, came to Great Neck as Lubavitch shluchim (emissaries) in 1990.' The same summer it marked its 25th anniversary with its new home at 400 East Shore Road (Long Island Press, 7 July 2016), counted from about 1991; it began as 'a small staff in a two-desk office'.

117904.name: The Chai Center
117904.note: Lubavitch.com: Rabbi Yaakov and Zoey Saacks 'arrived in 1993 and began activities in the living room of their home'. Medium: CrownHeights.info (18 Dec 2010) reports a 12 Dec 2010 banquet for their '18 years' (so 1992); its building went up in 1998.
